title: No-Churn Watermelon Sorbet
changes_from_base: Frozen watermelon chunks processed with yoghurt, a little sugar and lemon replace the mango purée and syrup; no ice-cream maker.
summary: No machine needed: frozen watermelon chunks whizzed with a little yoghurt, sugar and lemon make an instant soft pink sorbet.
equipment: baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: watermelon flesh, seeds removed, cut in 3 cm chunks (from a small 2000 g melon)

steps.title: Freeze the melon
steps.text: Spread the chunks in one layer on the lined tray, so they do not stick together, and freeze for at least 4 h, until hard.

steps.title: Process
steps.text: Tip the frozen chunks into the food processor with the yoghurt, sugar and lemon juice and pulse, then run, scraping down the sides, just until smooth. Stop before it turns slushy.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Spread it in the dish and freeze for about 1 h, until it holds a scoop. Eat the same day.

tips: Freeze the chunks spread apart so they do not freeze into one block.
Stop processing as soon as it is smooth; overworking makes it watery.
Add a few mint leaves to the processor for a fresh twist.
storage: Best eaten the day it is made; it freezes very hard. If frozen overnight, soften for 20 min and process again briefly.
